_comment: H2 (docs/design/1.6.0-TRACKER.md): 'conformance rigs carry one cell per Teller step per plane'.
Steps are ARCHITECTURE.md #2.2 (arrival, decode, authenticate, verify, approve, admit, route,
meter, audit, exit). This is the plane x step MATRIX: for every cell, either an id that names a
real, run scenario in one of the conformance rigs (or the shadow oracle, for the llm plane), or
the literal string "none" naming a genuine gap. 'gating' marks the 7 steps whose contract H2
spells out explicitly (a refusal/outcome that must never leak past its step); the other 3
(arrival, decode, approve) are mapped for completeness but do not fail the --check by themselves
when a shared, plane-agnostic kernel cell already covers them for every plane at once.
Checked by: scripts/teller-steps-check.py --check. Wired into scripts/verify-1.6.0-done.sh

decode.note: testing/voice-conformance/legs/spec-per-dialect.sh; the per-dialect spec battery includes decode-shape checks

authenticate.note: testing/voice-conformance/legs/provider-credential.sh; K1 -- credential threaded from the composition root before a session opens

verify.note: same leg also proves the mounted door can reach a real realtime provider -- VerifiedDestination in voice terms

approve.note: testing/voice-conformance/legs/session-scope.sh; K3 -- the session scope kind is a gate, not vocabulary

admit.note: testing/voice-conformance/legs/admit-refusal.sh; a key whose budget is already spent is refused AT THE DOOR (StartError::BudgetRefused, topology::open_admitted_session) before any host-side lease opens and before any ledger posting -- no provider dial has anything left to reach; a negative control (the same destination, uncapped) opens cleanly

route.note: testing/voice-conformance/legs/route-failover.sh; a hard-down provider dial trips the breaker cell on its first strike (topology::dial_provider), and the tripped cell refuses every FURTHER dial before any socket/URL work -- the documented terminal outcome, with no repeated egress once the cell is open

meter.note: testing/voice-conformance/legs/metering-lease.sh; K2 -- the session's money hop is the host's reserve-then-settle lease, capped by the caller's own budget

audit.note: testing/voice-conformance/legs/audit-record.sh; one governed session lands exactly one new admin-audit entry (topology::open_admitted_session -> VoiceRuntime::audit_session -> JournalHost::audit_record), carrying the voice.session.open action literal and the applied outcome; two sessions land exactly two rows

exit.note: testing/voice-conformance/legs/exit-terminal.sh; one session ends once -- a metering lease settles exactly once under a double close (LeaseCloseGuard's own idempotent cost_close contract), and a session's one admin-audit row survives being torn down before it ever runs a frame

decode.note: a malformed body is rejected before any admin operation runs -- the admin plane's own wire-shape check

authenticate.note: no credential on the admin listener -> 401 envelope, before any operation runs

verify.note: the operator admin credential presented at the DATA listener is not a valid signed vkey on the `keys` chain; refused before Admit ever draws a budget bucket -- the credential cannot reach a destination it was never scoped to reach

approve.note: same cell as verify: the closest genuine proof this harness can produce. A real insufficient-SCOPE 403 needs a role-bound EXTERNAL admin identity provider (busbar-core's admin-tokens principal is exempt/full by definition and cannot be capped); the harness only proves the auth-oidc plugin loads (plugins.load|auth-oidc), not a working token-issuing flow, so a scope-ceiling refusal is not exercised today

admit.note: the Config rate class (10 mutating calls/min) refuses the 11th call in one boot's window before the reload itself runs

route.note: an invalid new config is refused outright; the atomic rebuild-and-swap never runs and the prior config stays live -- the down-lane-ends-terminal outcome, admin-style

meter.note: one mutating admin op (PostGroups) leaves /api/v1/admin/usage at its fresh-boot zero shape -- admin operations are never billed, even under the oracle's non-zero per-request fee

audit.note: the fresh 4-op chain (mint, rotate, revoke, config/settings write): each mutating op seals exactly one new audit entry, right action/outcome, chain-linked

exit.note: the same Idempotency-Key replayed returns the first response verbatim -- one terminal per mutation, never doubled
